title: Kingdoms & domains
examples: How many main groups do we use to classify living things?
What is the difference between a kingdom and a domain?
Can you give an example of a prokaryote?

explain.say: We classify living things into groups to study them.

items: It makes huge amounts of data manageable

explain.say: The broadest grouping is the Domain, which is the highest level.
The next level down is the Kingdom, which groups similar life forms together.

items: Plantae: Plants that make their own food
Animalia: Animals that eat other things

explain.say: A concrete example of a plant is a tree because it has roots and leaves.
A concrete example of an animal is a dog because it moves and eats other things.
In the real world, we use this to understand where an organism fits.

faq.q: What is the difference between a kingdom and a domain?
faq.a: The Domain is the highest level of classification, grouping life into three major types. Kingdoms are groups below that, like plants or animals.
asks: How many levels are there in classification?
What is the biggest group of life?

faq.a: Yes, bacteria are prokaryotes, meaning they do not have a true nucleus inside their cells. This is a key feature.

faq.q: Do all plants belong to the Kingdom Plantae?
faq.a: Generally, yes, most plants are placed in the Kingdom Plantae. They are characterized by making their own food using sunlight.
asks: What is the defining feature of plants?

faq.q: What is the role of Fungi in an ecosystem?
faq.a: Fungi are important decomposers. They break down dead organic matter, which helps recycle nutrients back into the soil.
asks: Do mushrooms make their own food?
What do fungi do to dead wood?

faq.q: What is the most basic level of classification?
faq.a: The most basic level is usually the species, which groups very closely related organisms. This is below the Kingdom level.
asks: What is the smallest group of life?
How do we group very similar animals?

facts: The three Domains are Archaea, Bacteria, and Eukarya.
Eukarya includes organisms with a membrane-bound nucleus.
Plantae are autotrophs, meaning they produce their own food.
Animalia are heterotrophs, meaning they must consume other organisms.

quiz.say: An organism has a nucleus and can make its own food. Which Kingdom does it most likely belong to?
quiz.why: The presence of a nucleus and the ability to make food points directly to the characteristics of the Plantae Kingdom.

wrong.0: Bacteria are prokaryotes and do not have a nucleus.
wrong.1: Fungi obtain nutrients by absorbing them, they do not photosynthesize.
wrong.3: Animals must eat other things and lack a nucleus in the way plants do.

quiz.say: Which group represents the highest level of classification?
quiz.why: The Domain is the broadest and highest level used to classify life forms.

wrong.0: Phylum is a more specific grouping used within a Kingdom.
wrong.1: Species is the most specific level, representing a group of closely related organisms.
wrong.3: Kingdom is a level below Domain, grouping similar life types.

quiz.say: A single-celled organism lacking a nucleus is most likely in which Domain?
quiz.why: Bacteria are prokaryotes, meaning they lack a membrane-bound nucleus, placing them in the Bacteria Domain.

wrong.0: Eukarya is defined by having a nucleus, which this organism lacks.
wrong.1: Fungi are complex organisms that belong to the Eukarya Domain.
wrong.3: Archaea are also prokaryotes, but Bacteria is a common example of this group.
